claims.text: Ultrasonic Additive Manufacturing using consolidated metal foils can repair high-value, hot-cracking-prone components.
The proposed UAM repair can restore or enhance microstructural integrity and mechanical performance relative to traditional fusion-weld repair.
High-entropy or refractory alloys are examples of alloys prone to fusion-weld-induced hot cracking.

UAM can deposit repair foils layer by layer at temperatures below 150°C using approximately 20 kHz vibrations, approximately 25 micrometre amplitude, light mechanical pressure, and an inert atmosphere.
Maintaining the repair temperature below 150°C ensures solid-state bonding.
The UAM process produces a mechanically interlocked layered structure with metal-metal interfaces.
Ultrasonic processing causes localized plastic deformation at the repair interfaces.
The localized interfacial deformation produces submicron grain refinement.
UAM produces seamless metallurgical bonding between deposited layers.
Ultrasonic vibrations induce severe localized plastic deformation and frictional heating.
Localized plastic deformation and frictional heating enhance atomic diffusion and metallurgical bonding across layers without melting.
Avoiding formation of a liquid phase prevents the hot cracking associated with fusion welding.
UAM-generated deformation refines the microstructure at repair interfaces.
The UAM-repaired zone will have interfacial bond strength at least comparable to, or better than, a conventional fusion-weld repair.
The UAM-repaired zone will resist crack propagation better than a conventional fusion-weld repair.
The UAM-repaired zone will have superior durability under aggressive service conditions compared with a conventional fusion-weld repair.
Melting during traditional fusion-weld repair predisposes the repair zone to hot cracking and non-equilibrium solidification.
Hot cracking and non-equilibrium solidification in fusion-weld repairs compromise microstructural integrity and service performance.
The proposed approach is applicable to localized repairs of high-value components made from hot-cracking-prone alloys.
Extremely high loads and very thick repair deposits may require additional UAM parameter optimization.
